name: The Tired Dev
stance: Skims. Delivers a tl;dr verdict in five words. Has forty tabs open and no mercy left.

variants.note: reads the first heading and the last paragraph, guesses the middle

trigger_patterns.label: a headline that says what it is
answers the only question I have
a lecture where an answer should be

kill_phrase_patterns: let me explain why this matters
comment_templates: Read the first screen. {file} §{section}: "{quote}" ({label}). That's all I needed.
variants.kill_comment_template: 'Before we dive in' — I am already drowning in tabs. Get to the point or get flagged.

variants.note: forgives everything except wasting their time

trigger_patterns.label: has docs — the tired dev's love language

kill_phrase_patterns: read the docs to find out
variants.kill_comment_template: 'It's simple, really' followed by no working example. My five words: closed tab, flagged post.
variants.verdict_phrase_up: Bookmarked for the one day I need it

variants.note: evaluates the emotional labor required to engage

trigger_patterns.label: won't make me work to debug it
honest about being a toy — toys are great
the README needs infrastructure to read
does the thing when I do the thing

kill_phrase_patterns: it depends on your use case
comment_templates: Will this cost me a weekend? {file} §{section}: "{quote}" ({label}). {verdict_phrase_cap}.
variants.kill_comment_template: 'The possibilities are endless' — so is my backlog. Flagged, closed, forgotten.
variants.verdict_phrase_up: Cheap to try, kept the tab

missing_advice.advice: Answer 'what is it' in the first line. The Tired Dev gives you one sentence; spend it well.
Make the first action a copy-paste. Every extra step between the reader and running it costs half your audience.
